jobs.title: Senior Pricing Strategy Analyst
jobs.description:
Reporting to a Pricing Strategy Manager, you will provide complex and comprehensive analysis supporting pricing strategies for our Grocery operating segment. You will focus on mainstream brands, using data-driven insights to guide list pricing, promotional strategy, and trade investments. You will partner across Revenue Growth Management and cross-functional teams to evaluate business performance, identify risks and opportunities, and recommend actions that drive volume, margin, and profitable growth.

A Taste of Your Responsibilities
- Be a central resource for pricing analysis, recommendations, and reporting across the Revenue Growth Management team and with cross-functional partners

- Perform advanced pricing analysis using multiple data sources to develop actionable recommendations on list pricing, promotional strategy, and trade investments

- Analyze market trends, product volume, margins, competitive pricing, commodity markets, and promotional tactics to identify opportunities and risks

- Translate complex data into clear insights, strategies, and presentations for leadership decision-making

- Partner with Sales, Finance, Brand, and Category teams to align pricing and trade strategies with broader business objectives

- Lead cross-functional efforts to implement new or enhanced pricing processes, tools, and methodologies

- Build and maintain reporting and measurement frameworks to monitor pricing execution and effectiveness

- Manage projects that leverage multiple data sources to support key pricing and trade initiatives

Ingredients Required for Your Success
- Bachelor’s degree required

- 3+ years of business experience, including at least 1 year in consumer packaged goods (CPG) or similar industry

- Experience in Pricing, Category Management, Category Buying, Sales, Brand Finance, or a related field

- Experience performing complex analysis using multiple data sources to support pricing and trade decisions

- Advanced skills in Excel, including pivot tables, formulas, and data analysis

- Experience building presentations in PowerPoint to communicate insights and recommendations

- Strong analytical thinking with the capability to synthesize large amounts of data into clear, actionable insights

- Experience collaborating across multiple teams to influence decision-making and drive results

Number of Days in Office: 4

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Plant Manager, you will lead manufacturing operations at our Centralia, Illinois facility while driving safety, quality, service, cost, and people development objectives. You will provide operational leadership, oversee production execution, support capital and continuous improvement initiatives, and partner with cross-functional teams to deliver business results and operational excellence.

- Drive operational performance and key performance indicators across the facility.

- Support strategic, operating, and capital planning processes.

jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Manager, Connected Worker
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Sr.   Director, Manufacturing Excellence,   you will own the strategy, roadmap, governance, and value delivery for Conagra’s Connected Worker ecosystem. You will connect business needs with technology solutions that improve frontline productivity, standard work, employee capability, and operational performance. You will lead the expansion of connected worker capabilities beyond digital documents through mobile enablement, training, change management, defect handling, device readiness, and future technology solutions that create measurable business value.

A Taste of Your Responsibilities
- Own the Connected Worker strategy, multi-year roadmap, enhancement process, and prioritization across manufacturing sites.
- Identify and evaluate new use cases that improve safety, quality, productivity, reliability, compliance, and employee experience.
- Translate operational needs into scalable digital solutions, deployment plans, and measurable improvement opportunities.
- Partner with Manufacturing Excellence, Operations, Maintenance, Environmental Health & Safety, Food Safety, Quality, Regulatory and Analytical, Sanitation, and other functions to embed connected worker tools into standard ways of working.
- Build alignment across Plant Operations, Manufacturing Excellence, Information Technology, Digital Technology, Human Resources Technology, Procurement, vendors, and senior leaders.
- Influence stakeholders across multiple functions and locations to resolve tradeoffs, establish ownership, and advance enterprise priorities.
- Serve as the business owner for the Connected Worker platform and related frontline applications, including defect handling capabilities where applicable.
- Establish and maintain governance processes for roadmap intake, standards, deployment, training, support, issue resolution, adoption, data quality, and value realization.
- Define business requirements and standards for mobile device utilization, application readiness, refresh planning, and frontline user support.
- Partner with Information Technology, Procurement, vendors, and plant teams to remove barriers and improve mobile technology adoption.
- Lead Connected Worker training strategy and collaborate with plant champions, functional leaders, Human Resources, Learning, Information Technology, and vendors.
- Develop scalable training materials, communications, standard work, and enablement plans that support deployments and platform enhancements.
- Lead vendor business reviews, roadmap discussions, enhancement prioritization, and performance discussions.
- Benchmark external organizations and industry practices to identify future technology opportunities and best practices.
- Lead enterprise deployment planning and sustain adoption through continuous improvement activities.
- Track adoption, training completion, user feedback, issue trends, and business impact to ensure value realization and continuous optimization.

Ingredients Required for Your Success
- Bachelor’s degree required.
- Travel 25-50%, dependent on business needs

- Experience leading enterprise initiatives across multiple functions, locations, and stakeholder groups.
- Experience translating business needs into technology-enabled solutions, product roadmaps, deployment strategies, and business cases.
- Strong communication, collaboration, and influence skills with experience engaging frontline employees, operational leaders, functional partners, vendors, and senior leaders.
- Experience supporting the adoption of frontline technology solutions, including training, change management, mobile device deployment, and support processes.
- Experience working with cross-functional teams to drive sustainable business results.

jobs.title: Sr. Continuous Improvement Specialist - Lean Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Asset, Standards, and Ownership Leader, you will support the deployment, governance, and continuous improvement of the Lean Supply Chain Pillar within the Conagra Performance System. You will partner with manufacturing sites, platform leadership, supply chain teams, and enterprise stakeholders to eliminate losses, strengthen standards, build organizational capability, and deliver sustainable operational performance. You will serve as a Lean Supply Chain subject matter expert, leveraging Lean methodologies, data analytics, performance management, and digital manufacturing tools to identify opportunities, prioritize improvement efforts, and accelerate business results across manufacturing and supply chain operations. This role requires up to 75% travel to manufacturing sites, corporate meetings, and company events.
A Taste of Your Responsibilities
- Support enterprise ownership, governance, standards, and maturity progression of the Lean Supply Chain Pillar.
- Align Lean Supply Chain initiatives with Manufacturing Excellence priorities and integrate work across Conagra Performance System pillars and enterprise systems.
- Lead and support continuous improvement initiatives that reduce losses, eliminate waste, and improve operational performance.
- Use performance data, loss analysis, root cause problem solving, and value stream methodologies to identify opportunities and deliver measurable results.
- Facilitate workshops, performance reviews, and cross-functional improvement activities that improve productivity, efficiency, and service levels.
- Develop and maintain scorecards, key performance indicator frameworks, reporting tools, and analytical solutions that support enterprise decision making.
- Translate complex manufacturing and supply chain data into actionable insights, risks, trends, and recommendations.
- Integrate Lean Supply Chain principles with digital manufacturing capabilities, data visualization, automation, and modern manufacturing technologies.
- Partner with operations, engineering, information technology, and digital teams to implement scalable, technology-enabled improvements.
- Identify opportunities to leverage advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, connected manufacturing technologies, and digital tools to improve visibility and decision making.
- Coach site and platform teams on Lean Supply Chain standards, methodologies, and best practices.
- Support training, workshops, playbooks, and leadership discussions that strengthen ownership and accountability.
- Lead change management efforts that drive adoption, sustainment, and continuous improvement of Lean systems and behaviors.
- Prepare and deliver presentations for senior leaders, Operations Leadership Teams, and enterprise stakeholders.
- Communicate performance trends, strategic priorities, and recommendations through clear, fact-based storytelling.

Ingredients Required for Your Success
- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business, Industrial Technology, Data Analytics, or a related field.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in Continuous Improvement, Lean Supply Chain, Manufacturing Excellence, Operational Excellence, or related disciplines.
- Demonstrated success applying Lean methodologies, structured problem solving, and performance metrics to deliver measurable business results.
- Strong analytical, communication, facilitation, stakeholder management, and executive presentation skills.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Power BI, PowerPoint, data visualization, and performance reporting tools.
- Experience influencing cross-functional teams, leading initiatives without direct authority, and driving adoption of enterprise standards.
- Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent continuous improvement credential preferred.
- Experience supporting multi-site Lean Supply Chain, Conagra Performance System, or Manufacturing Excellence deployments preferred.
- Experience leveraging digital manufacturing, Industry 4.0 technologies, smart manufacturing, or advanced analytics to improve operational performance preferred.
- Familiarity with enterprise resource planning systems, manufacturing execution systems, Power Platform, Power BI, artificial intelligence-enabled analytics, predictive analytics, and digital performance management systems preferred.

jobs.title: Finance Director, Network Optimization
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Senior Director, Supply Chain Finance you will develop and evaluate financial plans and policies for assigned responsibilities. You will lead efforts to promote and incorporate best practices and benchmarks to improve processes and efficiencies. You will partner with the business to provide recommendations and help ensure sound financial decisions are made. You will lead a team of analysts and managers while supporting strategic supply chain and network optimization decisions.

A Taste of Your Responsibilities
- Perform financial analysis and evaluation of network optimization projects, including complete cash flow and project return analysis across multiple scenarios while incorporating all aspects of total delivered cost.
- Create and apply discounted cash flow models to evaluate and compare investment scenarios.
- Develop and interpret sensitivity analyses appropriate to each business situation.
- Own and maintain discounted cash flow models, synergy models, and other analytical tools, including determining the most appropriate methodology for each analysis.
- Conduct strategic decision support and investment analysis.
- Identify, validate, and gather required data to estimate ongoing savings and one-time costs.
- Determine critical assumptions, ask the right business questions, and incorporate relevant inputs into financial evaluations.
- Partner with Supply Chain Finance, Network Modeling, Mergers & Acquisitions, Brand Finance, Manufacturing Operations, Co-Manufacturing, Warehousing, Engineering, Sales and Operations Planning, Procurement, Transportation, and Project Management teams.
- Assess manufacturing overhead impacts, production throughput, staffing requirements, wage and utility rates, capital investments, avoided capital spending, delivered materials, tax incentives, working capital impacts, transportation and warehousing impacts, and accounting implications.
- Support the supply chain productivity agenda through financial evaluation, savings validation, performance tracking, forecasting, and reporting of productivity initiatives and results.
- Build effective working relationships across all organizational levels, from analysts to executive leadership.
- Train and mentor others on the use of advanced financial modeling tools and methodologies.
- Track and forecast project performance and develop reporting for leadership teams.
- Lead, coach, and develop a team while supporting their professional growth and career development.

Ingredients Required for Your Success
- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Supply Chain, or related field
- Master of Business Administration and/or Certified Public Accountant designation preferred.
- 10+ years of financial experience with strong preference for supply chain finance experience.
- Demonstrated success working independently in a fast-paced environment.
- Experience navigating ambiguity, organizational change, and evolving business priorities.
- Strong understandng of financial systems, general accounting concepts, and cost accounting principles.
- Demonstrated critical thinking skills and experience leveraging analytics, benchmarking, and insights to develop business strategies and solutions.
- Experience partnering across multiple functional areas to complete projects and solve business challenges.
- Background in profit and loss management and knowledge of financial and operating systems preferred.
- Proven success building strong partnerships with internal stakeholders and maintaining effective working relationships.
- Experience communicating actionable, forward-looking financial insights, business impacts, and potential risks to business partners.
- Cross-functional business experience preferred.
- Experience with SAP or similar enterprise software platforms preferred.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and SharePoint.

jobs.title: FP&A Internship - Summer 2027
jobs.description:
Have   a taste for something big? Launch your career at Conagra Brands, one of North America’s leading branded food companies!

Job Description

Our internship program will introduce you to the world of consumer-packaged goods with the goal of cooking up an interest in future career opportunities and allowing you to make an impact in a refuse-to-lose environment. Come work for a company known for iconic brands: Reddi-wip, Slim Jim, Angie’s BOOMCHICKPOP, Swiss Miss and more!

What Can You Expect from Your Internship?

You will be immersed   into   Conagra Brands and our Finance Organization for   11 weeks . The Corporate FP&A Intern performs analyses and reporting under general supervision. You can expect to work collaboratively with other members of the Conagra Corporate FP&A Team and Finance organization. To enhance your overall understanding of our company, we will provide opportunities to network with peers and leaders to gain experience with the scope of career paths available at Conagra Brands.

When:   May 2 4   – August   6 , 202 7

Location(s):   Chicago, IL , remote work is not   permitted

Schedule:   Interns should expect to work   40 hours /week

Why should you become a Conagra intern?

- Intern compensation starts at $2 3 / hr

- We set you up for success! All interns   participate   in two days of orientation in Omaha.

- You’ll   receive professional development guidance before and during the internship.

- Network with and learn from leaders across the company.

- Participate in Summer Hours, with the office closing at 1 p.m. on Friday.

- Summer relocation and housing   is   provided by Conagra as needed.

- Summer Send Off. Come back to Omaha to celebrate and give back to the community.

Is this internship right for you?

We're   looking for someone who wants to be part of promoting the most energized, highest impact culture in the food industry. If you are craving an opportunity to make a difference and   be   empowered to kick start your professional career in a refuse-to-lose environment, then we want to meet you! We encourage you to discover your   potential   and we will provide you with unparalleled opportunities to make a difference.

Do you   have   what it takes?

- You are enrolled in a degree program with at least 1 semester   remaining   after the internship program concludes

- A Planned   Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance   required

- You are willing to   relocate   to Chicago, IL for the duration of your internship

We want you to bring your whole self to work and value diversity and inclusion:

- Named a Best Place to Work multiple years by Human Rights Campaign’s Corporate Equality Index for LGBTQ+

- One of the Best Places to Work for Disability Inclusion by The Disability Equality Index

- Top company for   LatinX   talent as named by Latino Leaders Magazine

- Multi-Year honoree of Civic 50, recognizing the nation’s 50 most civic-minded companies

- Scholarship provider to Thurgood Marshall and Hispanic Scholarship Foundation

This job posting is an “Evergreen Requisition” designed to gather talent for current or future open positions. It Is a way for Conagra to   expedite   the hiring process when there is a need to fill that type of role. By applying to an Evergreen Requisition, you are expressing your interest in a particular job function within Conagra. Your application will be reviewed by a Talent Acquisition Specialist who may reach out to learn more about your career interests, and how that may best fit with Conagra. In addition to   submitting   your resume to an Evergreen Requisition, we encourage you to create a job search agent to be alerted when positions in your areas of interest become available.

Hourly Rate: $20-28

Our Intern Benefits
As a Conagra intern, you get paid holidays, relocation and housing assistance. During your time with us, you’ll have access to learning and development live sessions, as well as tools like LinkedIn Learning. You will also travel to our Omaha campus for Intern Orientation as well as an End of Summer Celebration. Our Company

Conagra Brands is one of North America's leading branded food companies. Guided by an entrepreneurial spirit, our Company combines a rich heritage of making great food with a sharpened focus on innovation. Our portfolio is evolving to satisfy people's changing food preferences. Our iconic brands, such as Birds Eye, Duncan Hines, Healthy Choice, Marie Callender's, Reddi-wip, and Slim Jim, and emerging brands, including Angie's BOOMCHICKAPOP, Duke's, Earth Balance, Gardein, and Frontera, offer choices for every occasion.

You will be immersed   into   Conagra Brands and our Finance Organization for   11 weeks . The Finance Modernization intern will create analytical tools using   cutting edge   software and partner with cross functional finance teams to advance analytical and reporting capabilities. You can expect to work collaboratively with other members of the Conagra Corporate FP&A Team and Finance organization. To enhance your overall understanding of our company, we will provide opportunities to network with peers and leaders to gain experience with the scope of career paths available at Conagra Brands.

We're   looking for someone who wants to be part of promoting the most energized, highest impact culture in the food industry. If you are craving an opportunity to make a difference and   be   empowered to kick start your professional career in a refuse-to-lose environment, then we want to meet you! We encourage you to discover your   potential   and we will provide you with unparalleled opportunities to make a difference.

Do you   have   what it takes?

- Cumulative GPA of 3.5 preferred

We want you to bring your whole self to work and value diversity and inclusion:

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Plant Manager, you will lead the day-to-day operations of plant production departments, including production and production planning. You will implement standard work and sustain continuous improvement through disciplined operating practices and autonomous maintenance. You will plan, organize, and coordinate production activities while leading multiple shift managers to support a safe, efficient operation that produces high-quality food products. You will partner closely with Human Resources, Continuous Improvement, Quality, and Finance to achieve operational, safety, quality, service, and cost objectives.

A Taste of Your Responsibilities
- Execute the plant's vision and mission to drive continuous improvement and alignment with company objectives.
- Direct and oversee production leaders across all shifts, ensuring accountability for performance and results.
- Drive employee engagement, training, and development programs to support manufacturing, quality, safety, and productivity goals.
- Communicate operational results, priorities, and action plans to employees and leaders throughout the facility.
- Partner with production planning and materials management teams to maximize schedule attainment and customer service.
- Collaborate with Human Resources to address and resolve employee relations matters effectively.
- Partner with Finance to develop and manage capital budgets and ensure financial commitments are achieved.
- Lead cost savings initiatives related to labor utilization, operational standards, and yield improvement.
- Support and advance the site's Total Productive Maintenance initiatives through close partnership with Continuous Improvement teams.
- Ensure all plant operations are conducted safely and in compliance with applicable requirements.
- Maintain and improve compliance with quality, food safety, regulatory, and company standards.
- Report food safety concerns through the appropriate channels and ensure timely resolution.

Ingredients Required for Your Success
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Industrial Management, Engineering, Food Science, Management, Product Operations, or a related field preferred
- Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered
- 5+ years of manufacturing experience.
- 3+ years of leadership experience in a management or supervisory capacity preferred
- Food industry experience within a unionized manufacturing environment preferred.
- Experience with Total Productive Maintenance initiatives preferred.
- Demonstrated success leading teams in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
- Experience driving employee development, engagement, operational excellence, and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Strong communication, presentation, negotiation, and analytical skills.
- Proficiency with business applications, financial management, budgeting, cost control, and statistical analysis.

Physical Requirements
More information about essential tasks and the facility will be shared during the hiring process. This role may require you to be in our manufacturing facilities. When visiting these sites, the physical requirements below may apply: You will be required to walk around the facility, climb stairs/ladders, kneel, or perform repetitive tasks that require hand-eye coordination. You may be required to lift or carry materials that can vary in weight and size. This is a manufacturing environment with large, moving equipment. Noise levels can be high, and temperatures may vary.

jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Manager (FI)
jobs.description:
As part of the Industrial Engineering Center of Excellence, reporting to the Director of Continuous Improvement - Industrial Engineering Focused Improvement, you will lead Focus Improvement initiatives to drive out loss across the network by identifying loss, guiding structured problem solving, and enabling collaboration across our manufacturing network. You will partner closely with plant teams and Manufacturing Excellence subject matter experts to drive cost reduction, efficiency, and scalable improvements while maintaining a strong on‑site presence at manufacturing facilities.
This position can be located in the following states:
AR, IN, KY, MI, MO MN, NE, IL, WI, OH

A Taste of Your Responsibilities
- Lead and support Focused Improvement initiatives aligned with network and enterprise objectives within the Industrial Engineering center of excellence.

- Partner with manufacturing sites to identify, prioritize, and eliminate chronic losses across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.

- Analyze multi‑site manufacturing data to identify trends, loss opportunities, and improvement priorities across multiple facilities.

- Apply structured problem‑solving methodologies such as Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control; Statistical Process Control; and Design of Experiments to deliver sustainable improvements.

- Coach site leaders and cross‑functional teams in Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, Unified Problem Solving, Work Process Improvement, Value Stream Mapping, loss trees, and root cause analysis.

- Develop financial justifications for optimization initiatives and capital projects, including return on investment and cost‑savings validation.

- Contribute to cross‑site initiatives focused on line performance, throughput, labor utilization, and equipment effectiveness.

- Collaborate with other Manufacturing Excellence pillars to align scope, share best practices, and prevent duplication of effort.

- Support the development of enterprise toolkits, playbooks, and standardized processes that enable knowledge transfer across the network.

- Partner with senior Focused Improvement leadership to assess, prioritize, and justify network‑wide improvement and capital opportunities.

- Communicate progress, results, and insights to site leadership and senior management audiences.

Ingredients Required for Your Success
- Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

- 7+ years of Industrial Engineering or continuous improvement experience in a manufacturing or supply chain environment.

- 4+ years of experience leading teams, programs, or large‑scale initiatives within manufacturing.

- Experience driving Total Productive Maintenance‑based continuous improvement initiatives in a plant environment.

- Demonstrated success developing and delivering continuous improvement programs that generate measurable, scalable value.

- Experience influencing and leading cross‑functional teams without direct reporting relationships.

- Strong financial acumen, including development of project cost justifications and capital evaluations.

- Experience presenting complex information to large audiences, including senior leadership.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Power BI for analysis and visualization and other related systems.

- Hands‑on experience with Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, Unified Problem Solving, and Work Process Improvement tools.

- Experience with Value Stream Mapping, line balancing, Statistical Process Control, and Design of Experiments.

- Manufacturing plant experience leading and supporting continuous improvement across multiple loss areas.

- Willingness to travel 60% or more to manufacturing sites depending on projects and proximity to plant locations.

Physical Requirements
More information about essential tasks and the facility will be shared during the hiring process. This role may require you to be in our manufacturing facilities. When visiting these sites, the physical requirements below may apply:
- You may be required to walk around the facility, climb stairs/ladders, kneel, or perform repetitive tasks that require hand-eye coordination.

- You may be required to lift or carry materials that can vary in weight and size.

- This is a manufacturing environment with large, moving equipment. Noise levels can be high, and temperatures may vary.
